findings.reason: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the whole safeParse result, so `{success, data}` gets written to credential.key, and googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) at line 75 then throws on the next construction; this runs on every Google refresh, whether or not sync is enabled.

Zod schemas have no custom toString, so both computed keys become "[object Object]" and the default strip mode drops expiry and other fields in sync mode, which breaks token persistence for callers such as Office 365.

Verified: in sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, so Google's `res?.data` is undefined (TypeError, swallowed by the catch), HubSpot writes the Response object into the key, and Zoho's `.data.error` throws.
Verified: zoho-bigin passes credentialId (credential.id) as the third argument, which is sent to the sync endpoint as calcomUserId, so tokens can be requested for the wrong user.

The Salesforce file has no prisma import, and globalThis.prisma is only assigned when NODE_ENV !== 'production', so the update throws a ReferenceError in production; it still type-checks because of the global declaration.

Verified: getClient now hits the token endpoint on every construction with no expiry check, skips refreshOAuthTokens, loses instance_url under the sync schema, and builds the Connection from the old credentialKey values; these are real but mostly efficiency or edge-case problems.

It is correct that parse, decrypt and JSON.parse throw without a catch and produce a 500, but this is a request for validation and error handling on an authenticated webhook, with no defect beyond the error code.

The secret is compared with !==, which is not constant-time, but a network timing attack is marginal; an unset secret cannot slip through because APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED requires the secret to be set.
